chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Marwazi, who said:

I heard him say: If you do not find someone to place the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) upon, then set it aside at that moment before the prayer. The charity is a sa' of dates, or its value in that land in dirhams.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: Dirhams, silver coins used as currency
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement used for Zakat al-Fitr
key_terms.قِيمَتِهِ: Its monetary value or equivalent price

ai.seo_question: What should one do with Zakat al-Fitr if no recipient is available before the Eid prayer?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from the chain of the Imams, clarifying that if no eligible recipient is found before the Eid prayer, the Fitrah is not immediately distributed but rather held in reserve until a qualified recipient appears. This highlights the Shia juristic view of Fitrah as a specific obligation tied to the Eid period, where the standard measure is one sa' of dates or its monetary value, ensuring the poor receive their due even if delayed slightly.
